title: First 48h Incident Resilience Slate
content:
Purpose:
This is an operational companion for launches: a compact, pragmatic 0-48h runbook focused on KPI signal interpretation, immediate mitigation steps, and staff/ownership mapping. Designed for product-ops + on-call + SRE to use in the first two days after a major rollout or traffic spike.

Scope:
- Applies to hosted API and Dedicated rollouts (hosted-api and dedicated product lanes).
- Focus on production KPIs that indicate systemic regressions (latency, error-rate, SLO burn, cost shocks).
- Not a full incident report; this is the tactical live-playbook for the first 48 hours. Post-48h: escalate to postmortem cadence and product review.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Monitor: P50/P95/P99 latency, 5xx rate, token cost burn, request throughput, queue depth, model-fallback counts.
- Trigger thresholds: P95 latency > 1.5x baseline OR 5xx > 0.5% sustained for 5m OR SLO burn hits 30% in 1h -> initiate Resilience Tier 1.
- Immediate actions: shift traffic to fallback model variant, enable prefix KV-cache whitelist for heavy endpoints, scale dedicated capacity pool if committed, open incident channel, notify product-ops commander.

KPI Tracker (live snapshot template - fill every 30m for first 6 hours, then hourly):
Headers: timestamp | p50_ms | p95_ms | p99_ms | 5xx_pct | success_pct | token_cost_usd/hr | queued_reqs | model_fallbacks | active_model | notes
Example row: 2025-02-22T09:00Z | 85 | 320 | 980 | 0.12 | 99.88 | 42.5 | 4 | 12 | gpt-redwood-v2-q4 | slight p95 increase on long sequences

Readiness Timeline & Checklist (owner initials in parens):
- D-14: Run synthetic smoke across major routes (priya) -> collect tail latency by seq-length bucket; update runbook thresholds.
- D-7: Finalize rollback objective and fallback model matrix (evan) -> mark compatible variants and quant profiles.
- D-3: Capacity dry-run: scale dedicated pool to +25% and run synthetic load for 90m (infra + eng-sre).
- D-1: Publish oncall rota and commander contact; confirm Playbook channel and rotation (product-ops).
- T-0 (deploy): Post deployment, start 5m cadence sampling for 30m with real-user traffic in observation mode; if any trigger fires, go to Tier 1.
- T+0-6h: Maintain 30m snapshots and update commander log; run sanity evals on top 10 prompts.
- T+6-24h: Hourly checks; move to daily cadence after 24h if stable.

Tiered Response (short):
- Tier 0 (observational): metric drift < trigger. Actions: notify, increase sampling, create incident iff drift persists > 1h.
- Tier 1 (mitigation): threshold crossed. Actions: open incident channel, set traffic weight to fallback model (20-50%), enable aggressive prefix caching, enable per-route timeouts, increase replicas or autoscale guard. Assign commander.
- Tier 2 (rollback/operational): multiple triggers or SLO burn > 50% in 1h. Actions: traffic cutback (50-100%), rollback to previous release, enable degraded-mode endpoints, escalate to exec on-call, open customer comms for affected customers.

Immediate play actions (copyable snippets for commander to paste into Slack / PagerDuty):
- "Incident opened: Tier 1. Observed p95 latency > threshold on routes /generation, fallback prepped. Assigning product-ops commander @Clara. All hands: check channel #launch-ops-thread-5678."
- "Operator action: shift route /chat to model=gpt-redwood-v2-quant-fallback weight=30% (ops-api:POST /routes/shift)."

Escalation matrix (who to call, order):
1) Product-ops commander: Clara Nguyen (oncall cell)
2) SRE lead: Miguel Alvarez
3) Serving runtime lead: Priya Shah
4) Eng infra: Evan Brooks
5) Customer success lead (if customers impacted): Riya Patel

Staffing rota snippet (first 48h):
- Hours 0-6: commander (Clara), SRE on-call (Miguel), runtime SME (Priya) - 3x primary responders
- Hours 6-18: handover to day shift: commander (backup: Evan), SRE (backup: Miguel second shift), support liaise (Riya)
- Hours 18-48: thinning: oncall + product-ops checkpoint every 4h; prepare summary for post-48h review.

Contingency playbook (triggers and actions):
- Trigger: sudden token_cost_usd/hr > 2x expected for high-traffic route.
  - Action: enable per-customer spending cap, triage top gen paths, enable shorter max_tokens on the route, throttle bulk requests.
- Trigger: model_fallback_count skyrockets (10x baseline)
  - Action: disable new model rollout traffic, run quick eval harness on fallback logs, if fallback performs worse -> rollback release.
- Trigger: queue depth > 50 for > 10m
  - Action: divert non-essential background jobs, enable emergency backpressure (return 429 for low-priority clients), scale worker pool.

What-if scenarios (short table of scenarios to rehearse):
- Scenario A: P95 latency spike driven by long-sequence user campaign -> mitigation: block known campaign prefixes, increase KV cache TTL for those prefixes, route long sequences to a lower-cost but higher-latency model while protecting SLAs.
- Scenario B: Gradual 5xx increase due to memory leak in runtime -> mitigation: restart smallest subset of nodes with canary weight 10%, monitor regressions, roll nodes forward on healthy behavior.
- Scenario C: Cost shock from embeddings route exploited by high-frequency calls -> mitigation: enable per-token-rate-limits, temp disable anonymous embeddings endpoint, notify CS for customer outreach.

Simulation plan (pre-launch rehearsals):
- Runbook dry-run schedule: D-7 full tabletop; D-3 live synthetic for 90m with injected faults (latency, 5xx, slow KV); D-1 command channel dry-run (message templates, snippets).
- Evaluation metrics for sims: mean time to detect (MTTD), mean time to mitigation (MTTM), percent of false positives, operator cognitive load notes.

Post-48h handover checklist:
- Create incident timeline artifact (owner: product-ops commander).
- Populate the KPI tracker with final 48h snapshot and attach to incident JIRA (OPS-1234).
- Schedule 48h postmortem + cross-team readout (product, infra, SRE, cs).

Open questions & notes to self:
- Should we default to fallback weight 30% or use traffic-based calculation? (prior note: 30% seems safe, but heavy traffic workloads may need 10-20% to reduce cost spike.)
- Verify automation for model-shift vs manual (evan to confirm API idempotency).
- Add a short script to populate KPI snapshot to a shared sheet for non-technical stakeholders (todo: Miguel).

Links & quick refs:
- Confluence playbook: https://confluence.redwood/projects/PRODOPS/pages/first-48h-playbook
- Incident ticket: JIRA OPS-1234
- Slack channel: #launch-ops-thread-5678
- Run synthetic harness: github.com/redwood/synthetic-load (runbook/README)

Commander log (scratch space - fill during incident):
[2025-02-22T09:05Z] - Observed p95 jump to 320ms; opened Tier 1.
[2025-02-22T09:11Z] - Shifted 30% traffic to gpt-redwood-v2-quant-fallback. p95 reduced to 200ms after 7m.
[2025-02-22T10:00Z] - Token cost spike persists on embeddings-route; enabled per-client throttles for anonymous clients.

Attachments to include in final incident: KPI-snapshots.csv, commander-log.txt, rollforward-decision-note.md

End of doc.
